regimen_profiles.regimen_role: High-risk or resistant gestational trophoblastic neoplasia
regimen_profiles.clinical_summary: High-risk GTN (FIGO score 7 or above), low-risk disease after failure or relapse following sequential single-agent therapy, or low-risk disease after methotrexate failure with hCG above 1,000 IU/L.
regimen_profiles.treatment_setting: High-risk or resistant gestational trophoblastic neoplasia
regimen_profiles.component_rationale: Dactinomycin — Interferes with the way tumour cells use DNA to make RNA. Etoposide — Prevents tumour cells repairing DNA during division. Methotrexate — Prevents rapidly dividing trophoblastic cells using folate to make new DNA. Folinic acid — Supplies a usable form of folate to protect healthy cells after methotrexate. Vincristine — Interferes with the structures that cells use to divide. Cyclophosphamide — Damages DNA so tumour cells cannot keep dividing.
regimen_profiles.schedule_context: Dactinomycin and etoposide are followed by methotrexate over 12 hours. Write down the infusion start time so you know when rescue begins. Return for dactinomycin and etoposide. Oral folinic acid starts today. The day 1 and 2 anti-sickness medicines form one course. Start the first oral folinic acid tablet 24 hours after the methotrexate infusion STARTS. Take four doses 12 hours apart unless your team gives you a different written rescue plan. If a tablet is late, missed or vomited, phone the unit straight away. Vincristine is given only into a vein, followed by cyclophosphamide. Tell the team about constipation or numbness before treatment. The full sequence repeats every 14 days.
key_points: Two treatment days in week one, oral rescue, then two different IV medicines on day 8.

Call your oncology unit urgently for fever, shaking chills or sudden illness. Call for severe constipation, abdominal pain, weakness, or a missed folinic acid dose. Report stinging at an IV site immediately.

Treatment continues to clear disease too small to detect. Low-risk disease usually needs three more courses. With high-risk disease the usual plan is three more cycles (six weeks), or four (eight weeks) with adverse features such as liver metastases.

The consultant may omit etoposide after hCG normalises to limit AML/MDS risk. G-CSF may preserve dose intensity. Minimise steroid exposure and review any day 2 omission or intensified folinic rescue with the GTN team.
Ask about persistent dry cough, new dyspnoea and fever at each review. Consider methotrexate pneumonitis alongside infection and assess promptly.

regimen_profiles.clinical_summary: Prevention of central nervous system involvement in high-risk GTN or low-risk GTN with lung metastases.
regimen_profiles.treatment_setting: Central nervous system prophylaxis in GTN
regimen_profiles.component_rationale: Methotrexate — Prevents rapidly dividing trophoblastic cells using folate to make new DNA. Folinic acid — Supplies a usable form of folate to protect healthy cells after methotrexate.
regimen_profiles.schedule_context: The specialist team gives methotrexate into the fluid around the spinal cord. There are three treatments two weeks apart. The team coordinates appointments with your systemic chemotherapy. Take the single prescribed oral folinic acid tablet 24 hours after the spinal dose. If you also have a separate methotrexate course, ask the team to write down both rescue schedules. Call immediately about a missed or vomited tablet.
key_points: One spinal treatment every 14 days for three doses, with an oral rescue tablet the following day.

Call your oncology unit urgently for fever, shaking chills or sudden illness. Seek urgent assessment for severe headache, fever, a stiff neck, new weakness, confusion or a seizure after spinal treatment.
Only the specialist team authorised to give intrathecal chemotherapy gives the spinal dose. Your oral rescue tablet and systemic medicines have separate routes and prescriptions.
Use a separate intrathecal prescription and the local authorised-personnel procedure. Coordinate with the systemic team. Vincristine is IV only and fatal by the intrathecal route.

Reconcile the three spinal doses with systemic therapy and all folinic acid orders. In low-risk GTN with lung metastases they accompany the first three methotrexate courses. In high-risk GTN they usually accompany the EMA block. Provide one reconciled rescue timetable.

Methotrexate — Prevents rapidly dividing trophoblastic cells using folate to make new DNA. Folinic acid — Supplies a usable form of folate to protect healthy cells after methotrexate. Cisplatin — Links strands of DNA together so tumour cells cannot divide normally.
regimen_profiles.schedule_context: Dactinomycin and etoposide are followed by a 12-hour methotrexate infusion. Record its start time. There is no second day of IV EMA in this regimen. Start the first oral folinic acid tablet 24 hours after the methotrexate infusion STARTS. Take four doses 12 hours apart unless your team gives you a different written rescue plan. The complete cycle repeats every two weeks.
key_points: EMA on day 1, folinic acid on days 2 and 3, then EP with fluids on day 8.
Call your oncology unit urgently for fever, shaking chills or sudden illness. Call promptly for reduced urine, ringing in the ears, new numbness, or missed rescue tablets.
Three further cycles over six weeks help treat disease too small to detect. Your consultant may extend this to four cycles over eight weeks when adverse features such as liver metastases are present.

On the day 8 cisplatin visit, check ability to maintain oral hydration. If nausea or vomiting precludes it, assess for IV hydration. Review concurrent nephrotoxic medicines and check for hearing or sensory changes before each cisplatin cycle.
